message.content:
**Sky‑Blue Pantone Codes**

There isn’t a single “official” Pantone value called *sky blue*—the term refers broadly to light, airy blues that resemble daylight over water. In practice designers choose from several close shades depending on how bright or muted they want it. Below are the most commonly used Pantone values that people refer to as “sky blue,” along with their approximate RGB/CMYK equivalents so you can see which might fit your project best:

| # | Pantone Code | Approximate Color |
|---|--------------|--------------------|
| **A** | **Pantone 290 C** | Very pale, almost pastel blue – often described as “baby blue.” |
| **B** | **Pantone 291 C** | Slightly deeper than 290 C, still very soft. |
| **C** | **Pantone 292 C** | A bit more saturated, closer to what many think of when picturing a clear daytime sky. |
| **D** | **Pantone 293 C** | Even richer, slightly teal‑tinted; good for high‑contrast designs where you still want a “blue‑in‑the-sky” feel. |

### Quick Reference Chart

```
Pantone   CMYK          RGB            Hex
--------------------------------------------
290 C     0–2–12–0      224–240–255    #E0F0FF
291 C     0–7–20–0      210–225–250    #D2E1FA
292 C     0–15–30–0     190–215–235    #BEDBEB
293 C     0–25–45–0     170–200–220    #AAD8DC
```

> **Tip:** If you’re printing, use the “C” (Coated) version because it gives a brighter result on glossy paper. For digital work, simply pick the hex/RGB equivalent above.

---

#### How to Pick One

| Situation | Recommended Shade |
|-----------|------------------|
| Light, subtle background | Pantone 290 C |
| Soft accent color | Pantone 291 C |
| Main body text/background | Pantone 292 C |
| Bold statement element | Pantone 293 C |

If none of those feels right, let me know the exact tone you’re after (e.g., cooler vs warmer, lighter vs darker). I can suggest additional Pantones such as 272 C (a mid‑tone sky blue) or even custom mixes using our `calculate_paint_mix` helper if you’d like to blend two colors together!
